reason: E1 shows that thermal exposure of a similar HEA coating (FeCoNiMnCu) at 800°C in air forms Cr2O3 and spinel oxides, enhancing wear resistance, which supports the oxide formation premise. E2 provides wear rate and friction data for the same coating under the exact conditions (15 N, 2 m/s) proposed, but it does not compare pre-oxidized vs. as-deposited states, so the predicted outcome of improved wear resistance from pre-treatment is not directly evidenced. The sluggish diffusion mechanism is not mentioned or supported by the cited passages.
premises: High-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu coatings is governed by a protective oxide layer.
The alloy's sluggish diffusion effect promotes formation of a stable, self-healing oxide film.
Thermal pre-treatment in air forms a coherent oxide scale containing Cr2O3 and spinel phases.
Pre-oxidized coatings will show lower wear rate and friction than as-deposited coatings at high temperature.
The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports oxide formation and wear behavior for this alloy system.
